statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; IPC s.201; IPC s.304-B; IPC s.498-A
aggravating_circumstances: Body chopped into two pieces and thrown in the park; blood stains found in matrimonial house; false explanation given by appellants; anti-mortem and post-mortem injuries indicating multiple perpetrators
trial_court_outcome: Husband, father-in-law and mother-in-law convicted; brother-in-law acquitted
offence_finally_established: Murder under IPC s.302 read with s.34
neutral_facts: The accused, who were the husband, father-in-law, and mother-in-law of the deceased, lived in a house where the deceased resided after her marriage. The deceased was found dead in the house, her body cut into two pieces and thrown in a park. Blood stains were found in the house, and the mother-in-law was seen disposing of the body by multiple witnesses. The autopsy report indicated that the crime could not have been committed by a single person, and the accused failed to explain how the deceased died. The accused claimed the deceased had gone to her relative's place and was missing, but this was proven false. The prosecution established a complete chain of circumstances linking the accused to the crime.
